extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and computer scientists (students and researchers) who write mathematical prose, proofs, and papers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and concrete rules for writing clear, readable mathematical text (papers, lecture notes, proofs) aimed at mathematicians and computer scientists. Emphasizes notation, sentence/paragraph structure, display equations, and editorial principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols in different formulas must be separated by words
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols in different formulas must be separated by words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write "$x_n$, $y_n$" not "$x_n y_n$" so readers can tell separate mathematical items apart; use words to separate symbols when they occur in sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't start a sentence with a symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't start a sentence with a symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recast the sentence or add a word so the sentence begins in natural language rather than with a bare mathematical symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use the same notation for two different things
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use the same notation for two different things. And don't use two different notations for the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent notation throughout a document; avoid reusing symbols for distinct concepts and avoid introducing multiple notations for a single concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give words between consecutive formulas (English glue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't compose a sequence of formulas with no intervening words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display formulas need English glue—use sentences to connect and explain displays so they form a coherent narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display unwieldy formulas; do not run them in
rubrics_metrics.description: Display unwieldy formulas; do not run them in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a formula takes more than about one-third of a line, place it on display rather than running it inline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuate displayed formulas as if they were ordinary words
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuate displayed formulas as if they were ordinary words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach commas, periods, semicolons to displayed equations so the surrounding sentences remain grammatically correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't omit 'the' with references
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't omit "the". "Equation 3", not "Equation 3"; prefer "the equation $x=y$."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use definite articles where appropriate in referring to equations, theorems, etc., to match natural English usage (prefer "the equation X").

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use 'any' when you mean 'every' or 'some'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use "any" when you mean "every" or "some".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with quantifiers: "any" can be ambiguous—choose "every" or "some" to convey the intended universal or existential meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using the same word in two different senses in the same paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of the same word in two different senses in the same paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent reader confusion by not shifting the meaning of a given word within a short span; if necessary, pick a different word or rephrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unfamiliar single words
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using even one word that will be unfamiliar to most readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer common vocabulary; if a technical or unusual word is necessary, define it before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary the sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary the sentence structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate long and short sentences (long, short, long, short) to keep prose engaging and readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use jargon that adds no information
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use jargon that adds no information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate filler phrases (e.g., "the fact that") which often mean "since" or "because"; be concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use parallel construction in parallel constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parallel construction in parallel constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing or coordinating elements, keep grammatical structure parallel for clarity and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-read what you wrote, often
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-read what you wrote, often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read drafts aloud to catch awkward phrasing, grammar issues, and clarity problems; iterative revision is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: State logical connectives explicitly in lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid lists of three with implicit "and" / "or".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting lists, explicitly state the connective ("and" vs "or") so the logical relationship is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer short familiar words over elaborate ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist the urge to use elaborate words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short familiar Anglo-Saxon words when possible; don't choose obscure or grandiose vocabulary when a simple word will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'we' appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The word "we" usually means "the author and the reader". Don't use "I"; don't be afraid of "we".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt "we" to create an inclusive exposition addressing author and reader jointly; avoid overuse of "I" in formal mathematical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number equations only if referenced
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't number an equation unless it is referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cluttering the paper with unused equation numbers; only label equations that will be cited later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't treat 'infinity' as a number
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't use the word "infinity" as if it were a number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise when discussing limits, extended reals, or unboundedness—treat ∞ conceptually, not numerically, unless using an extended number system with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparison symbols correctly and consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the symbols < > ≤ ≥ correctly and don't mix them in one chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid chains like a < b ≤ c < d that mix strict and non-strict inequalities in confusing ways; be consistent and explicit about inequality types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italicize variables; don't italicize numerals or function names
rubrics_metrics.description: Italicize variables; do not italicize numerals or function names like sin, log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow typographic conventions (variables in italics, standard function names upright) for readability and professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use real punctuation marks in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Use real punctuation marks in math mode (Knuth uses TeX so this is precise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure punctuation in mathematical formulas is correctly typeset and functions syntactically as part of surrounding sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display equations should be readable when surrounding text is masked
rubrics_metrics.description: Display equations should be readable when the surrounding text is masked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each displayed equation should be understandable on its own (have proper notation and context) so readers skimming displays can follow the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undefined acronyms
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undefined acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out acronyms at first use and ensure they are familiar to the reader before subsequent abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the theorem before proving it
rubrics_metrics.description: State the theorem before proving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present propositions, theorems, lemmas clearly and completely before launching into proofs so the reader knows what is being proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful with logical words ('if','iff','implies','only if')
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful with the words "if", "iff", "implies", "only if".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical connectives precisely; mistakes here cause semantic errors in mathematical claims—prefer explicit logical structure when ambiguity is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implicit subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid implicit subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear who or what performs an action in a sentence (e.g., instead of "Adding x to both sides yields...", state what is adding and whose sides are intended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes are usually evidence of bad writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes are usually evidence of bad writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If content in a footnote is essential to the reader's understanding, move it into the main text; use footnotes sparingly for genuinely peripheral remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations belong inline, not floating
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations belong inline, not floating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place references where the cited material is mentioned rather than clustering or leaving citations detached from the text they support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't write 'the author' when you mean 'I'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't write "the author" when you mean "I".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer first-person or inclusive "we" rather than awkward third-person self-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Halmos's rules (see Halmos for examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: See the Halmos rules; the Stanford lectures distilled them with examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Paul Halmos's well-known advice on mathematical exposition (clarity, economy, directness); consult Halmos's list for complementary stylistic maxims and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut adjectives and adverbs first in revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut adjectives and adverbs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In editing, remove unnecessary modifiers early to tighten prose and eliminate verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move definitions to the point of first use
rubrics_metrics.description: Move definitions to the point of first use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce definitions where they are needed rather than far in advance to reduce cognitive load and improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace nested negatives with positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace nested negatives with positives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite sentences like "not uncommon" or "it is not the case that" into positive formulations to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert nominalizations back to verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert nominalizations back to verbs ("a proof of the convergence" → "we prove the convergence").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer verbs over noun-heavy constructions to create more active, direct prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each paragraph has one theme and the first sentence states it
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paragraph has one theme; the first sentence states it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure paragraphs so that topic sentences introduce the theme and subsequent sentences develop it; avoid multi-theme paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections should follow the order: motivation→definitions→results→proofs→examples→applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections follow the order: motivation → definitions → results → proofs → examples → applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize sections to motivate problems before introducing technicalities, present theorems before proofs, and give examples and applications after results to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemmas should be motivated by the theorem they prepare
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemmas should be motivated by the theorem they prepare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce lemmas with an explanation of how they contribute to the main result so they don't appear as isolated technicalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: A reference the reader cannot find should not be cited
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference that the reader cannot find should not be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all citations are accessible and correct; do not cite obscure or unavailable works without providing necessary guidance or quotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put required material from footnotes into the text
rubrics_metrics.description: A footnote that the reader needs to read should be in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If content in a footnote is essential to understanding, include it in the main narrative rather than relegating it to a note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut footnotes that the reader does not need to read
rubrics_metrics.description: A footnote that the reader does not need to read should be cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate peripheral footnotes that clutter the page and do not add value to the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reader is your friend
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reader is your friend, not your adversary, not your judge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a helpful, cooperative tone in exposition: aim to guide and support the reader through the material rather than to show off or punish them with obscurity.
